input: Write a due diligence memo on Databricks

team.claim: Founders (aggregator): Ali Ghodsi, Ion Stoica, Matei Zaharia, Patrick Wendell, Reynold Xin, Andy Konwinski, Arsalan Tavakoli-Shiraji.
Ali Ghodsi is co-founder and CEO — company press release.

Executives (The Information org chart): Ion Stoica co-founder & Executive Chair; Matei Zaharia co-founder & CTO; Hatim Shafique COO; Andy Kofoid leads sales and marketing; Tram Phi SVP & General Counsel.
Board of directors includes Ion Stoica, Ali Ghodsi, Matei Zaharia, Ben Horowitz (a16z), Elena Donio (ex-Twilio), Pete Sonsini (NEA), Jonathan Chadwick (ex-VMware), Scott Shenker (UC Berkeley).
Five of the seven co-founders still had day-to-day roles at Databricks as of April 2025; a sixth sits on the board.

Notable departure: Naveen Rao, head of AI (joined via the 2023 $1.3B MosaicML acquisition), left to launch an AI-computer startup in September 2025; Databricks said he moves to an advisory role and will invest in his new venture (Bloomberg).
No successor for the head-of-AI role had been named as of Sept 13, 2025; analysts split on the impact of Rao's exit (InfoWorld).
Notable departure: Anil Bhasin, VP India & SAARC, exited Jan 15, 2025 to join a cybersecurity venture (TechCircle).
Departure: Drew Herd, who led the Google Cloud partnership for almost 6 years, announced his departure (~May 2026, LinkedIn post).
Amy Reichanadter is Chief People Officer (named in company response to Glassdoor reviews; aggregator data).

funding.claim: Series J: announced raising $10B (incl. non-dilutive financing; $8.6B completed at announcement) at a $62B valuation, led by Thrive Capital, co-led by Andreessen Horowitz, DST Global, GIC, Insight Partners and WCM Investment Management.

Series K term sheet: raising over-subscribed $1B at a valuation above $100B, backed by existing investors; closed per Sept 8, 2025 release, co-led by Andreessen Horowitz, Insight Partners, MGX, Thrive Capital and WCM (21a230b6).

Series L / Dec 2025 round: investments in excess of $7B including ~$5B equity at a $134B valuation plus ~$2B debt capacity; credit facilities led by JPMorgan Chase with Barclays, Citi, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley.
July 16, 2026 term sheet for a strategic round at a $188B valuation.

Aug 13, 2026: closed a $5B strategic round at a $190B valuation, led by Coatue with Blackstone, MGX, T. Rowe Price accounts and new investor Sixth Street Growth; new investors also BOND, Clearlake, Point72, Premji Invest, TPG.
Databricks reportedly raised ~$5B in debt from lenders Blackstone, Apollo Global Management and Blue Owl Capital — its largest debt raise ever (per Bloomberg, reported Jan 2025).
Secondary-market signal (aggregator, Clarity data): implied valuation $228.17B at $308.41/share as of Nov 8, 2026; total funding $25.55B across 15 rounds.

output.verdict: Databricks looks strong on commercial momentum: a $7B revenue run-rate growing >80% (company claim, Aug 2026), 20,000+ organizations including 70% of the Fortune 500, and a $5B round at a $190B valuation led by Coatue. What needs a closer look: the tripling of valuation in 20 months on unaudited, self-disclosed run-rates whose growth leans on existing-customer consumption, an unresolved AI copyright class action and recurring patent litigation, and the unquiet internal picture (work-life-balance scores, the head-of-AI exit with no named successor, and unverified layoff claims).

business.claim: Sells the Databricks Data + AI Platform: a unified platform for data engineering, warehousing, analytics and AI (products include Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, Unity Catalog) — company claim.
Business model (Sacra estimate/aggregator): B2B consumption-based SaaS priced in Databricks Units (DBUs), pay-as-you-go tied to compute/processing, with premium and enterprise tiers.
Platform operates natively across AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud; categories: enterprise software, data intelligence (aggregator page).
Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe — company claim.
Industries served: telecommunications, media & entertainment, financial services, public sector, healthcare & life sciences, retail, manufacturing — company site.
Built on an open-source foundation; founded by the original creators of the lakehouse, Apache Spark, Delta Lake, MLflow and Unity Catalog — company claim.

Geography expansion: plans to invest more than US$350 million in Singapore to expand AI operations; also targeting growth in Abu Dhabi/Middle East and doubled NYC office at 5 Bryant Park (news tracker/aggregator).

Pricing (G2 aggregator): starts at $99 per feature/month (Basic), no permanent free tier; production use requires negotiated enterprise agreement; DBU pricing sits on top of underlying AWS/Azure/GCP cloud costs.

traction.claim: Company claim: more than 20,000 organizations worldwide use the platform, including 70% of the Fortune 500.
Company claim: named customers include adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian and Unilever.
Company claim: over 1,000 customers consume at more than $1M revenue run-rate and over 100 customers at more than $10M run-rate.
Company claim: more than 15,000 customers around the world (Series K release); named customers Block, Comcast, Condé Nast, Rivian, Shell.
Company claim: net retention rate sustaining above 140%.
Company claim: launched or expanded partnerships with Microsoft, Google Cloud, Anthropic, SAP and Palantir in the prior two quarters.
Databricks and Microsoft extended their strategic partnership through the 2030s, deepening Azure integration (July 23, 2026).
Fox Corporation selected Databricks as strategic partner for its next-generation data and AI platform (press release Oct 13, 2026).
HP is moving its Customer Data Platform into Databricks, expected to yield a 40% cost reduction for HP (news tracker, Oct 2026).
Company claim (June 2026 summit blog): Marketplace partner solutions from 30+ ISVs; Databricks Apps grew 5x year over year with 5,000+ accounts running Apps weekly.
Partnerships (Sacra aggregator): multi-year, minimum $100M OpenAI partnership with GPT-5 natively available; native Google Gemini integration; SAP and Palantir partnerships.
Acquisitions (per partner guide citing releases): MosaicML $1.3B (2023), Neon (May 2025, press reports ~$1B), Tecton (Aug 2025), Row Zero (Sep 24, 2026), Electric/PGlite (Aug 2026).

red_flags.claim: Active AI copyright class action against Databricks/MosaicML proceeding in N.D. Cal. after motion to dismiss denied.

Valuation tripled from $62B (Dec 2024) to $190B (Aug 2026) in 20 months via five rounds — 'an IPO cadence'; headline figures are unaudited run-rates disclosed at fundraising moments (partner guide analysis).
Growth is driven largely by existing customers consuming more: run-rate rose ~75% while customer count rose ~one-third between Sep 2025 and Aug 2026 ('part of that 80% is your invoice').
Round size ballooned beyond plan: wanted to raise $1B, investors offered $15B, settled on $5B at $190B; $20B raised in the prior 20 months (TechCrunch).
Head of AI Naveen Rao departed Sep 2025 with no named successor as of the article date — a succession gap in the AI roadmap.

2025 incident: a stolen credential was used to access and manipulate a cloud-hosted Databricks workspace (per BeyondTrust disclosure); plus an audit-log session-token exposure patched in Oct 2025 (08dc329b).
Unverified employee claims on Blind of layoffs of new hires right before vesting (Oct 2025 review); no company-confirmed layoff numbers found.
Customer complaint of ~10x cost overage vs the pricing calculator with partial refund only, consistent with broader G2 reviews calling DBU pricing opaque.

reputation.claim: Glassdoor (aggregator): 4.0/5 from 1,713 reviews; 92% approve of CEO Ali Ghodsi; rating down 3% over the last 12 months; Best Places to Work winner 2022, 2025, 2026.
Glassdoor category scores: work/life balance 3.3 and senior management 3.7 are the weakest; AI review summary cites intense work pressure, burnout reports and mixed feedback on leadership.
Glassdoor demographic gaps (aggregator): people with disabilities 2.2 stars (16 ratings), Hispanic/Latinx 3.0 (25), LGBTQ+ 3.2 (14), women 3.6 vs men 4.1.

Blind (aggregator): 3.8/5 from 946 reviews; lowest score work/life balance 3.0; recent reviews (Oct-Nov 2026) cite 'brutal deliver or out culture' and internal politics, while praising compensation and CEO.

Customer complaint pattern (G2 review, Dec 16, 2025): reviewer says the pricing calculator was wrong ~10x, paid over 10x expected cost, received only a partial refund after Databricks denied responsibility.
Capterra (aggregator): 4.5/5 (28 reviews); recurring criticisms are cost unpredictability at scale, cluster startup delays and learning curve.
Critical press: InfoWorld ran 'Databricks at a crossroads: can its AI strategy prevail without Naveen Rao?' questioning the AI roadmap after the head-of-AI departure.

missing_fields: Audited financial statements (private company; only self-reported run-rates/FCF available)
Regulatory enforcement actions or sanctions exposure (none found in collected court/regulator-adjacent sources)
Company-confirmed headcount and layoff figures (only aggregator estimates and unverified employee claims)

financial_signals.claim: Company claim: crossed a $7B revenue run-rate with >80% year-over-year growth in Q2 (announced Aug 13, 2026).
Run-rate trajectory (company claims): expected >$3B in quarter to Jan 31, 2025; >$4B (+50%) Sep 2025; >$4.8B (+55%) Dec 2025; >$5.4B (+65%) Feb 2026; >$7B (+80%) Aug 2026.
Company claim: Lakehouse data-warehousing product surpassed $1.5B run-rate, growing >100% YoY; Lakebase surpassed $100M run-rate.
Company claim: AI products crossed a $1.4B revenue run-rate (Feb 2026).
Company claim: positive adjusted free cash flow over the last 12 months (run-rate, growth and FCF are unaudited company disclosures).
Third-party estimate (Sacra, aggregator): $7B annualized revenue in July 2026, ~80% YoY growth in Q2 2026; free-cash-flow positive for full year 2025; gross margins 70-80% (Sacra estimate).
Headcount trend (aggregators): ~7,100 employees as of July 2024 (The Information) vs ~10,000 employees as of Oct 2026 (stockanalysis.com / ai.lounge.ai) — ~40% growth.
Hiring: new office leases signed in San Francisco and Sunnyvale to attract AI talent (company claim).
Layoffs signal (unverified employee claim on Blind, Oct 2025): 'Layoffs of new hires right before vesting; I've seen this happen to a large number of colleagues.'
Investing.com analysis: the $190B valuation implies ~27x the $7B run-rate revenue.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: AI copyright class action: a California federal judge (N.D. Cal.) denied Databricks/Mosaic ML's motion to dismiss on Apr 22, 2026, letting claims that authors' books were used to train LLMs proceed (Law360).

The same copyright suit (plaintiffs include Rebecca Makkai, Jason Reynolds, Abdi Nazemian) alleges MosaicML used the Books3 dataset to train its MPT model and Databricks' DBRX LLM; Judge Charles B. Dreyer said plaintiffs' allegations are sufficient.

Patent suit: Poulin Holdings, LLC v. Databricks, Inc., No. 4:26-cv-00245 (E.D. Tex.), filed Mar 10, 2026; Databricks answered Jun 18, 2026 and moved to transfer venue to N.D. Cal. on Aug 13, 2026; docket active as of Nov 6, 2026 (PacerMonitor docket).

Databricks sued patent-monetization firm Ascend IP and founders (W.D. Wash., No. 2:24-cv-01417) alleging an 'extortion scheme' of nuisance patent claims; separately Byteweavr has a pending patent suit against Databricks in Texas federal court, which Databricks denies (Reuters).

Security incident (2025): BeyondTrust publicly described threat activity in which an actor used a stolen credential to access a cloud-hosted Databricks workspace, removed IP access rules, added a malicious IP allow rule and ran queries (aggregator breach timeline).

Vulnerability (Oct 2025): BeyondTrust found unredacted JSESSIONID session tokens in Databricks Unity Catalog audit logs enabling session hijacking; Databricks promptly patched the issue (BeyondTrust blog).

TeamPCP supply-chain attack: in Mar 2026 researchers alleged possible Databricks compromise; Databricks investigated and stated on Apr 1, 2026 it 'thoroughly investigated... and found nothing' (security tracker).
No regulatory enforcement actions, sanctions exposure or regulator fines for Databricks were found in the collected sources.
